condition: Alternative to re-alignment

text: For conformity of production verification of the change in vertical position of the cut-off line under the influence of heat, one of the sampled lamps or systems shall be tested according to the procedure of Annex 7 paragraph 3.1 after being subjected three consecutive times to the cycle described in Annex 7 paragraph 3.2.2.
A headlamp or system shall be considered acceptable in conformity of production if Δr of the cut-off line does not exceed 1.5 mrad upwards and does not exceed 2.5 mrad downwards.

If Δr of the headlamp or system exceeds 1.5 mrad but is not more than 2.0 mrad upwards or exceeds 2.5 mrad but is not more than 3.0 mrad downwards, a second sample shall be tested and the mean of the absolute values recorded on both samples shall not exceed 1.5 mrad upwards and 2.5 mrad downwards.
condition: if the first sample's Δr is between 1.5 and 2.0 mrad upwards or between 2.5 and 3.0 mrad downwards

text: If the mean value of 1.5 mrad upwards and 2.5 mrad downwards on the two headlamps or systems is not complied with, another two systems shall be subjected to the same procedure and Δr for each of them shall not exceed 1.5 mrad upwards and 2.5 mrad downwards.
condition: if the two-sample mean criterion is not met

text: A front fog lamp shall be considered acceptable in conformity of production if Δr of the cut-off line does not exceed 3.0 mrad.

If Δr of the front fog lamp exceeds 3.0 mrad but is not more than 4.0 mrad, a second front fog lamp shall be tested and the mean of the absolute values recorded on both samples shall not exceed 3.0 mrad.
condition: if the first front fog lamp's Δr is between 3.0 and 4.0 mrad

text: In conformity of production, the chromaticity coordinates of road illumination devices shall be complied with.
The conformity requirements shall be considered satisfied from a mechanical and geometric standpoint if the differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.

With respect to photometric performance, conformity of mass-produced lamps shall not be contested if, when testing any lamp chosen at random equipped with a standard (étalon) light source and/or non-replaceable light source(s) and/or light source module(s) as present in the lamp, no measured value deviates from the values prescribed in paragraph 6 of this Regulation.
In the case of a lamp equipped with a replaceable light source, if the photometric test results do not meet the requirements, tests on lamps shall be repeated using another standard light source.
condition: lamp equipped with a replaceable light source and results not meeting requirements

text: If the conformity test results do not meet the requirements, the alignment of the lamp may be changed only according to the provisions of Annex 5 paragraph 4.1.
condition: if test results do not meet the requirements

text: For AFS, if the conformity test results do not meet the requirements, the alignment of the system may be changed in each class according to Annex 5 paragraph 4.1; this does not apply to lighting units as indicated under paragraph 5.3.3.1.1.
condition: if test results do not meet the requirements

text: Lamps with apparent defects shall be disregarded in conformity of production testing.
For each type of lamp the holder of the approval mark shall carry out at least the tests specified in Annex 2, at appropriate intervals, in accordance with the provisions of this Regulation.

If any sampling shows non-conformity with regard to the type of test concerned, further samples shall be taken and tested, and the manufacturer shall take steps to ensure the conformity of the production concerned.
condition: if sampling shows non-conformity

text: Conformity tests by the manufacturer shall cover the photometric and colorimetric characteristics and the verification of the change in vertical position of the cut-off line under the influence of heat.
Conformity tests shall generally be carried out in accordance with the methods set out in this Regulation.

In conformity tests carried out by the manufacturer, equivalent methods may be used only with the consent of the competent authority, and the manufacturer shall prove that the applied methods are equivalent to those of this Regulation.
condition: if equivalent methods are used

text: Test apparatus used for conformity tests shall be regularly calibrated and correlated with measurements made by a competent authority.
In all cases the reference methods shall be those of this Regulation, particularly for administrative verification and sampling.
Samples of lamps shall be selected at random from the production of a uniform batch, and the assessment shall in general cover series production from individual factories.
A manufacturer may group together records concerning the same type from several factories only if these operate under the same quality system and quality management.
condition: if records from several factories are grouped

text: The sampled devices shall be subjected to photometric measurements at the points provided for in the Regulation, with readings limited as specified in Annex 2 paragraph 2.4.1.

For driving-beam headlamps of Classes A and B, the CoP photometric readings shall be taken at points Imax, HV, H-3L and H-3R; when the driving-beam is reciprocally incorporated with the passing-beam, HV of the driving-beam shall be the same measuring point as for the passing-beam.
For asymmetrical passing-beam headlamps of Classes C, V and AFS, the CoP photometric readings shall be taken at points B50L (or R), 50L (or R), 50V, 75R (or L) if applicable and 40R (or L).
For Class AS headlamps, the CoP photometric readings shall be taken at points HV, 3.43°D/5°L and 3.43°D/5°R.

For Class BS headlamps, the CoP photometric readings shall be taken at points Imax and HV for the driving-beam (HV being the same point as for the passing-beam when reciprocally incorporated), and at points HV, 0.86°D/2.5°R and 0.86°D/2.5°L for the passing-beam.
For Classes CS and DS headlamps, the CoP photometric readings shall be taken at points Imax and HV for the driving-beam and at point 0.86°D/V for the passing-beam.
For front fog lamps, the CoP photometric readings shall be taken at points 8 and 9 and lines 1, 5, 6, 8 and 9 as specified in Table 19.
For cornering lamps, the CoP readings shall be taken at points P1, P2 and P3 as specified in Table 18 and the required chromaticity coordinates shall be checked.
The manufacturer shall carry out a statistical study of the test results and define, in agreement with the competent authority, criteria governing the acceptability of his products.
The acceptability criteria shall be such that, with a confidence level of 95%, the minimum probability of passing a spot check in accordance with Annex 3 (first sampling) would be 0.95.
In sampling by an inspector, the conformity requirements shall be considered satisfied from a mechanical and geometric standpoint if the differences do not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.

In sampling by an inspector, conformity of mass-produced lamps shall not be contested if, when testing any lamp chosen at random equipped with a standard (étalon) light source and/or non-replaceable light source(s) and/or light source module(s) as present in the lamp, no measured value deviates from the values prescribed in paragraph 6 of this Regulation.
In sampling by an inspector, for a lamp equipped with a replaceable light source whose results do not meet the requirements, tests shall be repeated using another standard light source.
condition: lamp with a replaceable light source and results not meeting requirements

text: Lamps with apparent defects shall be disregarded in sampling by an inspector.
In the first sampling four lamps shall be selected at random; the first sample of two is marked A and the second sample of two is marked B.

Conformity of mass-produced lamps shall not be contested if the deviation of any specimen of samples A and B (all four lamps) is not more than 20 per cent; if the deviation of both lamps of sample A is not more than 0 per cent the measurement can be closed.

Conformity shall be contested if the deviation of at least one specimen of samples A or B is more than 20 per cent; the manufacturer shall be requested to align production and a repeated sampling shall be carried out within two months after notification.
condition: deviation of at least one specimen of A or B more than 20 per cent

text: Samples A and B shall be retained by the Technical Service until the entire COP process is finished.
condition: if conformity is contested after first sampling

text: In the first repeated sampling four lamps shall be selected at random from stock manufactured after alignment; the first sample of two is marked C and the second D.

Conformity shall not be contested if the deviation of any specimen of samples C and D (all four lamps) is not more than 20 per cent; if the deviation of both lamps of sample C is not more than 0 per cent the measurement can be closed.

If one specimen of samples C or D deviates by more than 20 per cent but all specimens deviate by not more than 30 per cent, conformity shall be contested, the manufacturer shall again be requested to align production, and a second repeated sampling shall be carried out within two months after notification.
condition: deviation of a specimen of C or D between 20 and 30 per cent

text: Samples C and D shall be retained by the Technical Service until the entire COP process is finished.
condition: if conformity is contested after first repeated sampling

text: If one specimen of samples C or D deviates by more than 30 per cent, the approval shall be withdrawn and paragraph 5 of Annex 3 shall be applied.
condition: deviation of a specimen of C or D more than 30 per cent

text: In the second repeated sampling four lamps shall be selected at random from stock manufactured after alignment; the first sample of two is marked E and the second F.

Conformity shall not be contested if the deviation of any specimen of samples E and F (all four lamps) is not more than 20 per cent; if the deviation of both lamps of sample E is not more than 0 per cent the measurement can be closed.
If the deviation of at least one specimen of samples E or F is more than 20 per cent, conformity shall be contested, the approval shall be withdrawn and paragraph 5 of Annex 3 shall be applied.
condition: deviation of a specimen of E or F more than 20 per cent

text: Approval shall be withdrawn according to paragraph 3.6 of this Regulation.
condition: when withdrawal is required by Annex 3

text: For verification of the change in vertical position of the passing-beam cut-off line under heat, one lamp or system of sample A shall be tested according to Annex 7 paragraph 3 after being subjected three consecutive times to the cycle of Annex 7 paragraph 3.2.2.
The passing-beam or system shall be considered acceptable if Δr does not exceed 1.5 mrad upwards and does not exceed 2.5 mrad downwards.

If Δr exceeds 1.5 mrad but is not more than 2.0 mrad upwards or exceeds 2.5 mrad but is not more than 3.0 mrad downwards, a second system of sample A shall be tested and the mean of the absolute values on both samples shall not exceed 1.5 mrad upwards and 2.5 mrad downwards.
condition: first sample Δr between 1.5 and 2.0 mrad upwards or 2.5 and 3.0 mrad downwards

text: If the 1.5 mrad upwards / 2.5 mrad downwards criterion on sample A is not complied with, two systems of sample B shall be subjected to the same procedure and Δr for each shall not exceed 1.5 mrad upwards and 2.5 mrad downwards.
condition: sample A criterion not met

text: A front fog lamp shall be considered acceptable if Δr does not exceed 3.0 mrad.

If the front fog lamp Δr exceeds 3.0 mrad but is not more than 4.0 mrad, the second front fog lamp of sample A shall be tested and the mean of the absolute values on both samples shall not exceed 3.0 mrad.
condition: first front fog lamp Δr between 3.0 and 4.0 mrad

text: If the 3.0 mrad criterion on sample A is not complied with, the two front fog lamps of sample B shall be subjected to the same procedure and Δr for each shall not exceed 3.0 mrad.
condition: sample A criterion not met

text: For photometric measurement the device or part(s) thereof shall be mounted on a goniometer with a fixed horizontal axis and a moveable axis perpendicular to the fixed horizontal axis.
Luminous intensity values shall be determined by means of a photoreceptor contained within a square of 65 mm side.

Except for cornering lamps, the photoreceptor shall be set up at a distance of at least 25 m forward of the centre of reference of each headlamp or lighting unit, perpendicular to the measurement axis from the origin of the goniometer.
condition: except cornering lamps

text: Angular coordinates shall be specified in degrees on a sphere with a vertical polar axis according to the gonio-photometer as defined in Figure A4-I.
During photometric measurements, stray reflections should be avoided by appropriate masking.
An equivalent photometric method may be used only if the applicable correlation is observed.
condition: if an equivalent photometric method is used

text: An aiming screen shall be used; it may be located at a shorter distance than the photoreceptor.
Before starting the measurements, the device or part(s) thereof shall be aimed as described in Annex 5.

Upon request of the applicant, for a matched pair of lamps the photometric requirements for each single measuring point, segment or zone apply to half of the sum of the respective measured values from both lamps together.
condition: upon request of the applicant, matched pair

text: For matched pairs, the division by the factor of 2 does not apply in the cases of paragraph 5.1.4.2 and the footnotes of Tables 5, 6, 14, 15, 16, 17 and 19 where a provision is specified for one side only.
condition: provisions specified for one side only

text: For AFS, any offset of the centre of reference of each lighting unit with respect to the goniometer rotation axes should be avoided, especially in the vertical direction and for lighting units producing a cut-off.

For AFS, the photometric requirements for each single measuring point or segment of a lighting function or mode apply to half of the sum of the respective measured values from all lighting units of the system applied for this function or mode.
For AFS, the division by the factor of 2 does not apply where a provision is specified for one side only: paragraphs 5.3.2.5.2, 5.3.2.8.1, 5.1.4.2, 5.3.3.4, 5.3.5.1 and notes 1 and 7 of Table 7.
condition: provisions specified for one side only

text: The lighting units of an AFS shall be measured individually; simultaneous measurements may be performed on two or more lighting units of an installation unit only if equipped with the same light source types with respect to power supply, their illuminating surfaces are completely contained in a rectangle of not more than 300 mm horizontal and 150 mm vertical extent, and a common centre of reference is specified by the manufacturer.
The AFS shall, prior to the subsequent test procedures, be set to the neutral state.
The AFS or part(s) thereof shall be aimed before starting the measurements so that the position of the cut-off complies with the requirements of Table 8.
Parts of an AFS measured individually and having no cut-off shall be installed on the goniometer under the mounting position specified by the applicant.
condition: parts measured individually having no cut-off

text: For cornering lamps, if measurement results are challenged, the distance of measurement shall be such that the law of the inverse of the square of the distance is applicable.
condition: in the event that measurement results are challenged

text: For cornering lamps, if measurement results are challenged, the measuring equipment shall be such that the angle subtended by the receiver from the reference centre of the light is between 10′ and 1°.
condition: in the event that measurement results are challenged

text: For asymmetric passing-beams, the test point locations for left-hand traffic shall be mirrored about the V-V line relative to those indicated for right-hand traffic.
condition: left-hand traffic

text: The aiming shall be carried out using a flat vertical screen set up at a distance of 10 m or 25 m (as indicated in item 9 of Annex 1) forward of the device and at right angles to the H-V axis.
The aiming screen shall be sufficiently wide to allow examination and adjustment of the device over at least 5° on either side of the V-V line.

The luminous intensity distribution of a principal passing-beam headlamp, or of at least one lighting unit for a class C passing-beam of an AFS, or of a front fog lamp in its neutral state shall incorporate a "cut-off".
For right hand traffic beams, the asymmetric "cut-off" line shall provide a straight "horizontal part" towards the left and a raised "elbow - shoulder" part towards the right.
condition: right hand traffic beams

text: For left hand traffic beams, the asymmetric "cut-off" line shall provide a straight "horizontal part" towards the right and a raised "elbow - shoulder" part towards the left.
condition: left hand traffic beams

text: In each case the "elbow-shoulder" part of the asymmetric "cut-off" line shall have a sharp edge.
The symmetric "cut-off" line shall provide a straight "horizontal part" towards the left and the right.

For a road illumination device designed to provide a driving-beam not adjustable independently from the passing-beam, measurements of the luminous intensity of the driving-beam shall be taken with the same alignment as for the measurements of the passing-beam, the passing-beam being aimed according to Annex 5 paragraph 3.2.
condition: driving-beam not adjustable independently from the passing-beam

text: A road illumination device providing a driving-beam adjustable independently from the passing-beam shall be so adjusted that the area of maximum luminous intensity is centered on the point of intersection of lines H-H and V-V.
condition: driving-beam adjustable independently from the passing-beam

text: A road illumination device providing a principal passing-beam headlamp of Class C or V, or at least one lighting unit for a class C passing-beam of an AFS, shall be visually aimed by means of the asymmetric "cut-off".

For vertical adjustment of a Class C or V passing-beam, the horizontal part of the "cut-off" is moved upward from below line B and adjusted to its nominal position one per cent (0.57°) below the H-H line.

For horizontal adjustment of a Class C or V passing-beam, the "elbow - shoulder" part of the "cut-off" shall be moved from right to left for right hand traffic or from left to right for left hand traffic.
After horizontal movement, above the line 0.2°D the "shoulder" of the asymmetric "cut-off" shall not exceed the line A to the left for right hand traffic or to the right for left hand traffic.
After horizontal movement, at the line 0.2°D or below the "shoulder" of the asymmetric "cut-off" should cross the line A.
After horizontal movement, the kink of the "elbow" of the asymmetric "cut-off" is basically located within +/-0.5° to the left or right of the V-V line.
In the case of a headlamp designed to provide bend lighting, its alignment may be changed only provided that the axis of the beam is not displaced vertically by more than 0.2°.
condition: headlamp designed to provide bend lighting

text: A road illumination device providing a principal passing-beam headlamp of Classes AS, BS, CS or DS shall be visually aimed by means of the symmetric "cut-off".

For vertical adjustment of a Class AS, BS, CS or DS passing-beam, the horizontal part of the "cut-off" is moved upward from below line B and adjusted to its nominal position one per cent (0.57°) below the H-H line, according to paragraph 3.2.1.1.
For horizontal adjustment of a Class AS, BS, CS or DS passing-beam, the cut-off line shall be so positioned that the projected beam pattern appears approximately symmetrical to the V-V line.
A road illumination device providing a front fog lamp of Class F3 shall be visually aimed by means of the symmetric "cut-off".
For vertical adjustment of a front fog lamp, the "cut-off" is moved upward from below line B and adjusted to its nominal position 1 degree below the H-H line.
For horizontal adjustment of a front fog lamp, the cut-off line shall be so positioned that the projected beam pattern appears approximately symmetrical to the V-V line.

When the front fog lamp is designed for use in pairs or has otherwise an asymmetric beam pattern, it shall be horizontally aligned according to the specification of the applicant, or otherwise in such a way that the cut-off line appears symmetrical to the V-V line.
condition: front fog lamp designed for use in pairs or with an asymmetric beam pattern

text: A road illumination device providing a cornering lamp shall be installed on the goniometer in the axis of reference according to paragraph 3.1.2.1. (a) and (b) of this Regulation.

Where a device designed to provide a passing-beam or a driving-beam not adjustable independently from the passing-beam does not meet the requirements of paragraphs 5. or 6.2. when aimed, its alignment may be changed only provided the axis of the beam is not displaced horizontally by more than 0.75° to the left or to the right.
condition: device aimed as described in paragraph 3 does not meet the requirements of paragraphs 5. or 6.2.

text: Where a device designed to provide a driving-beam adjustable independently from the passing-beam does not meet the requirements of paragraphs 5. or 6.2. when aimed, its alignment may be changed only provided the axis of the beam is not displaced horizontally by more than 1° to the left or to the right.
condition: device aimed as described in paragraph 3 does not meet the requirements of paragraphs 5. or 6.2.

text: Where a device designed to provide a front fog lamp or a cornering lamp does not meet the requirements of paragraphs 5. or 6.2. when aimed, its alignment may be changed only provided the axis of the beam is not displaced horizontally by more than 2° to the left or to the right.
condition: device aimed as described in paragraph 3 does not meet the requirements of paragraphs 5. or 6.2.

text: Where a device designed to provide a passing-beam or a driving-beam not adjustable independently from the passing-beam does not meet the requirements of paragraphs 5. or 6.2. when aimed, its alignment may be changed only provided the axis of the beam is not displaced vertically by more than 0.25° up or down.
condition: device aimed as described in paragraph 3 does not meet the requirements of paragraphs 5. or 6.2.

text: Where a device designed to provide a driving-beam adjustable independently from the passing-beam does not meet the requirements of paragraphs 5. or 6.2. when aimed, its alignment may be changed only provided the axis of the beam is not displaced vertically by more than 0.5° up or down.
condition: device aimed as described in paragraph 3 does not meet the requirements of paragraphs 5. or 6.2.

text: Where a device designed to provide a front fog lamp or a cornering lamp does not meet the requirements of paragraphs 5. or 6.2. when aimed, its alignment may be changed only provided the axis of the beam is not displaced vertically by more than 0.5° up or down.
condition: device aimed as described in paragraph 3 does not meet the requirements of paragraphs 5. or 6.2.

text: Where a driving-beam not adjustable independently from the passing-beam, aimed as described in paragraph 3, does not meet the requirements of paragraph 5.1. or 6.2., the alignment of the device may be changed with respect to the passing-beam first aiming.
condition: driving-beam not adjustable independently does not meet paragraph 5.1. or 6.2.

text: Where an AFS aimed as described in paragraph 3 does not meet the requirements of paragraph 5.3. or 6.2., the alignment of the system may be changed in each class independently with respect to the first aiming.
condition: AFS does not meet paragraph 5.3. or 6.2.

text: If vertical adjustment of a device providing a passing-beam or a front fog lamp cannot be performed repeatedly to the required position within the tolerances of Annex 5 paragraph 4.1., the instrumental method of Annex 6 shall be applied to test compliance with the required minimum quality of the "cut-off" and to perform the vertical and horizontal adjustment of the beam.
condition: vertical adjustment cannot be performed repeatedly within tolerances

text: The instrumental aiming method shall be applied to test the minimum quality of the "cut-off" and to perform vertical and horizontal beam adjustment only if the vertical adjustment of the device providing a passing-beam or a front fog lamp cannot be performed repeatedly to the required position and tolerances described in Annex 5.
condition: vertical adjustment cannot be performed repeatedly within Annex 5 tolerances

text: Where instrumental aiming applies, the quality of the "cut-off" line shall be tested according to Annex 6 paragraph 2.2. and the instrumental vertical and horizontal adjustment of the beam shall be performed according to Annex 6 paragraph 2.3.
condition: Annex 6 paragraph 1.2. applies

text: Before carrying out the measurement of the quality of the "cut-off" and the instrumental aiming procedure, a visual pre-aim in accordance with the device specific paragraph(s) of Annex 5 is required.
condition: Annex 6 paragraph 1.2. applies

text: To determine the minimum sharpness of the "cut-off", measurements shall be performed by vertically scanning through the horizontal part of the "cut-off" in angular steps of 0.05° at either 10 m with a detector of approximately 10 mm diameter or 25 m with a detector of approximately 30 mm diameter.
The measuring distance at which the cut-off quality test was carried out shall be recorded in item 9. of the communication form (Annex 1).

To determine the maximum sharpness and linearity of the "cut-off", measurements shall be performed by vertically scanning through the horizontal part of the "cut-off" in angular steps of 0.05° exclusively at a measurement distance of 25 m with a detector having a diameter of approximately 30 mm.
The "cut-off" quality shall be considered acceptable if the requirements of Annex 6 paragraphs 2.2.1. to 2.2.3. are complied with in at least one set of measurements.
Not more than one "cut-off" shall be visible.

The sharpness factor G = (log Eβ - log E(β + 0.1°)) shall be determined by scanning vertically through the horizontal part of the "cut-off" at 2.5° from the V-V line for a passing-beam with asymmetric "cut-off" line.

The sharpness factor G = (log Eβ - log E(β + 0.1°)) shall be determined by scanning vertically through the horizontal part of the "cut-off" at 2.5° left and right from the V-V line for a passing-beam and front fog lamp with symmetric "cut-off" line.
For a passing-beam designed to provide an asymmetric "cut-off" line, the sharpness factor G shall not be less than 0.13 (minimum sharpness).
For a passing-beam and front fog lamp designed to provide a symmetric "cut-off" line, the sharpness factor G shall not be less than 0.08 (minimum sharpness).
For a passing-beam designed to provide an asymmetric "cut-off" line, the sharpness factor G shall not be greater than 0.40 (maximum sharpness).

For a passing-beam designed to provide an asymmetric "cut-off" line, the part of the horizontal "cut-off" that serves for vertical adjustment shall be horizontal between 1.5° and 3.5° from the V-V line.
For a passing-beam and front fog lamp designed to provide a symmetric "cut-off" line, the part of the horizontal "cut-off" shall be horizontal between 3° left and right from the V-V line.
The inflection points of the "cut-off" gradient at the vertical lines at 1.5°, 2.5° and 3.5° shall be determined by the equation d2 (log E) / dβ2 = 0.
For a passing-beam designed to provide an asymmetric "cut-off" line, the maximum vertical distance between the determined inflection points shall not exceed 0.2°.
For a passing-beam and front fog lamp designed to provide a symmetric "cut-off" line, the maximum vertical distance between the determined inflection points shall not exceed 0.5°.
The beam adjustment may be performed instrumentally only if the "cut-off" complies with the quality requirements of Annex 6 paragraph 2.2.
condition: cut-off complies with quality requirements of paragraph 2.2.

text: For instrumental vertical adjustment of a passing-beam headlamp with asymmetric "cut-off" line, a vertical scan moving upward from below line B is carried out through the horizontal part of the "cut-off" at 2.5° from the V-V line, on the left side for right hand traffic and on the right side for left hand traffic.

For instrumental vertical adjustment of a passing-beam and front fog lamp with symmetric "cut-off" line, a vertical scan moving upward from below line B is carried out through the horizontal part of the "cut-off" on the V-V line.
For a passing-beam headlamp, the inflection point (d2 (log E) / dβ2 = 0) is determined and positioned on the line B situated 0.57° (1 per cent) below the H-H line.
For a front fog lamp, the inflection point (d2 (log E) / dβ2 = 0) is determined and positioned on the line B situated 1° below the H-H line.
For horizontal adjustment of a passing-beam headlamp with asymmetric "cut-off" line, the applicant shall specify one of the horizontal aim methods: the "0.2°D line" method or the "3 line" method.

In the "0.2°D line" method, a single horizontal line at 0.2°D shall be scanned from 5° left to 5° right after the lamp has been aimed vertically, and the maximum gradient G = (log Eβ - log E(β + 0.1°)), β being the horizontal position, shall not be less than 0.08.
condition: applicant specifies the 0.2°D line method

text: In the "0.2°D line" method, the inflection point found on the 0.2°D line shall be positioned on the line A.
condition: applicant specifies the 0.2°D line method

text: In the "3 line" method, three vertical lines shall be scanned from 2°D to 2°U at 1°R, 2°R and 3°R after the lamp has been aimed vertically, and the respective maximum gradients G = (log Eβ - log E(β + 0.1°)), β being the vertical position, shall not be less than 0.08.
condition: applicant specifies the 3 line method

text: In the "3 line" method, the inflection points found on the three lines shall be used to derive a straight line, and the intersection of this line with the line B found during vertical aim shall be placed on the V line.
condition: applicant specifies the 3 line method

text: For instrumental horizontal adjustment of a passing-beam headlamp or front fog lamp with symmetric "cut-off" line, the cut-off line shall be so positioned that the projected beam pattern appears approximately symmetrical to the V-V line.

For front fog lamps designed for use in pairs or otherwise having an asymmetric beam pattern, the "cut-off" line shall be horizontally aligned according to the specification of the applicant, or otherwise in such a way that the cut-off line appears symmetrical to the V-V line.
condition: front fog lamp designed for use in pairs or with asymmetric beam pattern

text: A complete sample of each road illumination device (except cornering lamps) shall be tested for stability of photometric performance in operation, once the photometric values have been measured.

For a headlamp with an asymmetrical passing-beam or AFS, the photometric values shall be measured beforehand at Imax for driving-beam and at points 40L, 50R, B50L for passing-beam (or 40R, 50L, B50R for left-hand traffic).

For a headlamp with a symmetrical passing-beam, the photometric values shall be measured beforehand at Imax for driving-beam, at points 0.50°U/1.5°L, 0.50°U/1.5°R, 50R, 50L for Class BS passing-beam, and at points 0.86°D-3.5°R, 0.86°D-3.5°L for Classes CS and DS passing-beams.
For front fog lamps, the photometric values shall be measured beforehand at the point of maximum illumination in zone D (Imax) and at the point HV.

For headlamps or front fog lamps, the complete sample tested shall be the complete lamp itself including ballast(s) and those surrounding body parts, light sources or light source module(s) which could influence its thermal dissipation.

For an AFS, the complete sample shall be the complete right and left side of the system including electronic light source control-gear(s) and/or supply and operating device(s) and those surrounding body parts and lamps which could influence its thermal dissipation; each installation unit and lamp(s) and/or light source module may be tested separately.

The stability tests shall be carried out in a dry and still atmosphere at an ambient temperature of 23 °C ± 5 °C, the test sample being mounted on a base representing the correct installation on the vehicle.

In case of replaceable light sources, the stability tests shall use mass production filament light sources aged for at least one hour, or mass production gas-discharge light sources aged for at least 15 hours, or mass production LED light sources and LED modules aged for at least 48 hours, cooled down to ambient temperature before starting the tests.
condition: replaceable light sources

text: The LED modules supplied by the applicant shall be used for the stability tests.
In the case of an AFS providing an adaptation of the driving-beam, the driving-beam shall be in the maximum condition if activated during the stability tests.
condition: AFS providing an adaptation of the driving-beam

text: The measuring equipment for the stability tests shall be equivalent to that used during type approval tests.
The AFS or part(s) thereof shall, prior to the stability tests, be set to the neutral state.
The test sample shall be operated without being dismounted from or readjusted in relation to its test fixture.
The light source used in the stability tests shall be a light source of the category specified for that headlamp.
For the stability of photometric performance test, the clean device shall be operated for 12 hours as described in Annex 7 paragraph 2.1.1. and checked as prescribed in Annex 7 paragraph 2.1.2.
condition: except cornering lamps

text: Where a device is designed to provide only one lighting function (driving-beam or passing-beam or front fog lamp) and not more than one class in case of passing-beam, the corresponding light emitting element(s) shall be lit for the time specified in paragraph 2.1. (12 hours).
condition: if the device provides only one lighting function

text: Where a device is designed to provide two or more lighting functions, it shall be subjected to a cycle of 15 minutes with the main mode lit and 5 minutes with all other functions intended by the manufacturer to be used simultaneously in the same body and which in combination draw the highest total wattage lit, until the specified time is reached.
condition: if the device provides two or more lighting functions

text: For a passing-beam designed to provide bend lighting with additional light source(s) or light source module(s), these shall be switched ON for one minute and OFF for nine minutes during activation of the passing-beam only; with several additional light sources for bend lighting, the test shall be carried out with the combination representing the most severe operating condition.
condition: if bend lighting is provided by additional light sources or light source modules

text: For a headlamp equipped with a cornering lamp with additional light source(s) or light source module(s), these shall be switched ON for one minute and OFF for nine minutes during activation of the passing-beam only.
condition: if the headlamp is equipped with a cornering lamp with additional light sources

text: Where the driving-beam uses several light sources and the applicant declares that a part of the driving-beam is used exclusively for short time 'flash to pass' signals, the test shall be carried out without this part of the driving-beam.
condition: if a part of the driving-beam is declared for flash to pass only

text: When the tested headlamp includes signalling lamps, these shall be lit for the duration of the test, except a daytime running lamp; a direction indicator lamp shall be lit in flashing mode with an on/off time of approximately one to one.
condition: if the tested headlamp includes signalling lamps

text: For replaceable filament light source(s) operated directly under vehicle voltage system conditions, the test shall be performed at 6.3 V, 13.2 V or 28.0 V as applicable; if the applicant specifies that the test sample may be used at a different voltage, the test shall be carried out with the filament light source operated at the highest voltage that can be used.
condition: replaceable filament light sources operated directly under vehicle voltage

text: For replaceable gas discharge light source(s), the test voltage for the electronic light source control-gear, or the light source where the ballast is integrated, is 13.2 ± 0.1 volts for 12 V vehicle voltage system, or otherwise as specified in the application for approval.
condition: replaceable gas discharge light sources

text: All measurements on lighting units equipped with non-replaceable light sources operated directly under vehicle voltage system conditions shall be made at 6.3 V, 13.2 V or 28.0 V or at other voltages according to the vehicle voltage system as specified by the applicant.
condition: non-replaceable light sources operated directly under vehicle voltage

text: For light sources operated independently from vehicle supply voltage and fully controlled by the system, or supplied by a supply and operating device, the specified test voltages shall be applied to the input terminals of that device.
condition: light sources supplied by a supply and operating device or fully controlled by the system

text: LED light source(s) and light source module(s) shall be measured at 6.3 V, 13.2 V or 28.0 V respectively, if not otherwise specified within the pertinent Regulation; those operated by an electronic light source control gear shall be measured as specified by the applicant.
condition: LED light sources and light source modules

text: Where signalling lamps grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated into the test sample operate at voltages other than the nominal rated voltages of 6 V, 12 V or 24 V, the voltage shall be adjusted as declared by the manufacturer for the correct photometric functioning of that lamp.
condition: if signalling lamps are incorporated and operate at non-nominal voltages

text: For a gas-discharge light source, the test voltage for the ballast, or for the light source where the ballast is integrated, is 13.2 ± 0.1 volts for 12 V network system, or otherwise as specified in the application for approval.
condition: gas-discharge light sources

text: Once stabilized to ambient temperature, the headlamp lens and external lens, if any, shall be cleaned with a clean, damp cotton cloth and inspected visually; no distortion, deformation, cracking or change in colour of either lens shall be noticeable.
condition: after the clean device stability test

text: For a headlamp with asymmetrical passing-beam, photometric values shall be verified after the stability test at 50R, B50L, 40L (right-hand traffic) or 50L, B50R, 40R (left-hand traffic) for the passing-beam and at Imax for the driving-beam; except for B50L, the discrepancy from values measured prior to the test shall not exceed 10 per cent including the tolerances of the photometric procedure.
For a headlamp with asymmetrical passing-beam, the value measured at point B50L after the stability test shall not exceed the photometric value measured prior to the test by more than 1.70∙10^2 cd.

For a Class BS headlamp, photometric values shall be verified after the stability test at 50R, 50L, 0.50°U/1.5°L and 0.50°U/1.5°R for the passing-beam and Imax for the driving-beam; except at 0.50°U/1.5°L and 0.50°U/1.5°R, the discrepancy from pre-test values shall not exceed 10 per cent including photometric tolerances.
condition: Class BS headlamps

text: For Classes CS and DS headlamps, photometric values shall be verified after the stability test at 0.86°D/3.5°R, 0.86°D/3.5°L, 0.50°U/1.5°L and 0.50°U/1.5°R for the passing-beam and Imax for the driving-beam; except at 0.50°U/1.5°L and 0.50°U/1.5°R, the discrepancy from pre-test values shall not exceed 10 per cent including photometric tolerances.
condition: Classes CS and DS headlamps

text: For a headlamp with symmetrical passing-beam, the value measured at points 0.50°U/1.5°L and 0.50°U/1.5°R after the stability test shall not exceed the photometric value measured prior to the test by more than 2.55∙10^2 cd.
condition: Classes BS, CS and DS headlamps

text: For front fog lamps, photometric values at point HV and Imax in zone D after the stability test shall not differ by more than 10 per cent from the values measured prior to the test, including the tolerances of the photometric procedure.

After the clean device test, the headlamp shall be operated for one hour for each function as described in paragraph 2.1.1. after being prepared with the test mixture as prescribed in paragraph 2.2.1., and checked as prescribed in paragraph 2.1.2.; a sufficient cooling down period must be assured after each test.

The test mixture shall be uniformly applied to the entire light-emitting surface of the headlamp and left to dry, repeated until the illumination value has dropped to 15-20 per cent of the values measured at: Imax in passing/driving-beam and driving-beam only; 50R and 40L for a passing-beam-only headlamp for right-hand traffic; 50L and 40R for a passing-beam-only headlamp for left-hand traffic.
condition: headlamp with asymmetrical beam pattern or AFS

text: For a Class BS headlamp, the test mixture shall be applied until the illumination has dropped to 15-20 per cent at Imax (passing/driving-beam and driving-beam only) or at 50L and 50R (passing-beam only).
condition: Class BS headlamps

text: For Classes CS and DS headlamps, the test mixture shall be applied until the illumination has dropped to 15-20 per cent at Imax (passing/driving-beam and driving-beam only) or at 0.50°U/1.5°L, 0.50°U/1.5°R and 0.86°D/V (passing-beam only).
condition: Classes CS and DS headlamps

text: For a front fog lamp, the test mixture shall be applied until the illumination at Imax in zone D has dropped to 15-20 per cent of the measured value.

The vertical drift of the cut-off line under the influence of heat shall not exceed the specified value for an operating headlamp producing a passing-beam, for front fog lamps, and for an AFS emitting a class C passing-beam or each specified passing-beam mode; the device tested per paragraph 2. shall be subjected to the test of paragraph 3.1. without being removed from or readjusted in relation to its test fixture.

If the AFS consists of more than one lighting unit or assembly of lighting units which provide a cut-off, each shall be tested separately as a test sample; with a moving optical part only the position closest to the average vertical angular stroke and/or the neutral state initial position is tested, with signal inputs corresponding to a straight road only.
condition: AFS

text: The cut-off drift test shall be carried out with the voltage adjusted as specified in paragraph 2.1.1.2., in a dry and still atmosphere at an ambient temperature of 23 °C ± 5 °C, with the device operated without being dismounted from or readjusted in relation to its test fixture.

The cut-off drift test shall use a mass production filament light source aged for at least 1 hour, mass production LED light source(s)/LED module(s) as submitted aged for at least 48 hours, or a mass production gas-discharge light source aged for at least 15 hours.

For a device with an asymmetrical beam pattern, the position of the cut-off line in its horizontal part (between V-V and the vertical through B50L for right-hand traffic or B50R for left-hand traffic) shall be verified 3 minutes (r3) and 60 minutes (r60) after operation.

For a headlamp with a symmetrical beam pattern, the position of the cut-off line in its horizontal part (between V-V and the verticals through 50L and 50R for Class BS, 3.5°L and 3.5°R for Classes CS and DS) shall be verified 3 minutes (r3) and 60 minutes (r60) after operation.
For front fog lamps, the position of the cut-off line between points 3.0° left and 3.0° right of V-V shall be verified 3 minutes (r3) and 60 minutes (r60) after operation.
The measurement of the variation in cut-off line position shall be carried out by any method giving acceptable accuracy and reproducible results.
For headlamps or AFS, the absolute value Δr1 = |r3 - r60| shall be not more than 1.0 mrad upward and not more than 2.0 mrad downward.
For front fog lamps, the absolute value Δr1 = |r3 - r60| shall be not more than 2.0 mrad.

If the result does not comply with paragraph 3.2.1. but does not exceed the values in Table A7-1, a further sample mounted on a test fixture representative of the correct vehicle installation shall be tested per paragraph 3.1. after three consecutive cycles of one hour operation (voltage per 2.1.1.2.) and one hour switched OFF, and shall be acceptable if its Δr values meet paragraph 3.2.1.
condition: if first result fails 3.2.1 but is within Table A7-1

text: Retesting of a further sample is only permitted if the upward movement of the cut-off of a headlamp or AFS does not exceed 1.5 mrad.
Retesting of a further sample is only permitted if the upward movement of the cut-off of a front fog lamp does not exceed 3.0 mrad.
Retesting of a further sample is only permitted if the downward movement of the cut-off does not exceed 3.0 mrad for all devices.

For devices with outer lens of glass, the dirt test mixture shall be composed of 9 parts by weight silica sand (particle size 0-100 μm), 1 part by weight vegetal carbon dust from beech wood (0-100 μm), 0.2 parts by weight NaCMC, 5 parts by weight sodium chloride (pure at 99 per cent) and an appropriate quantity of distilled water with conductivity ≤ 1 mS/m.
condition: outer lens made of glass

text: The dirt test mixture shall not be more than 14 days old, and the NaCMC used shall have a degree of substitution of 0.6-0.7 and a viscosity of 200-300 cP for a 2 per cent solution at 20 °C.

For devices with outer lens of plastic material, the dirt test mixture shall be composed of 9 parts by weight silica sand (0-100 μm), 1 part by weight vegetal carbon dust from beech wood (0-100 μm), 0.2 parts by weight NaCMC, 5 parts by weight sodium chloride (pure at 99 per cent), 13 parts by weight distilled water with conductivity ≤ 1 mS/m and 2 ± 1 drops by weight of surfactant; the mixture shall not be more than 14 days old.
condition: outer lens made of plastic material

text: A test report shall be prepared covering the tests and results of Annex 8 tests 3.1. to 3.5., added to the documentation for the device for approval, noting the road illumination device used for the test.
condition: except cornering lamps

text: Every application for approval shall be accompanied, for the test of the plastic lens material, by fourteen lenses.
condition: except cornering lamps

text: Ten of the lenses may be replaced by ten material samples only if at least 60 mm x 80 mm in size, with a flat or convex outer surface and a substantially flat area (radius of curvature not less than 300 mm) in the middle measuring at least 15 mm x 15 mm.
condition: if material samples replace lenses

text: Every lens or sample of material submitted shall be produced by the method to be used in mass production.
The application shall be accompanied, if applicable, by an optical assembly to which the lenses can be fitted in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions.
condition: if applicable

text: For testing the UV-resistance of plastic light transmitting components against UV radiation of LED modules inside the headlamp, one sample of each relevant material or one device sample containing these shall be submitted, each material sample having the same appearance and surface treatment as intended for use; not necessary if only low-UV-type LED modules per Annex 9 are applied or the components are shielded from UV radiation, e.g. by glass filters.
condition: unless only low-UV LED modules are used or UV shielding is provided

text: The samples supplied pursuant to Annex 8 paragraph 1.2. shall satisfy the requirements of Annex 8 paragraphs 3.1. to 3.6.
condition: except cornering lamps

text: The two samples of complete road illumination devices incorporating lenses of plastic material shall, with regard to the lens material, satisfy the requirements of Annex 8 paragraph 3.7.
condition: except cornering lamps

text: The samples (lenses of plastic material or samples of material) shall be subjected, with the optical assembly to which they are intended to be fitted where applicable, to approval tests in the chronological order indicated in Table A8-1.

Tests of paragraphs 3.1. to 3.5. need not be repeated only if the lamp manufacturer proves that the product has already passed them or equivalent tests under another regulation; the tests prescribed in Table A8-2 shall be mandatory.
condition: if prior compliance with tests 3.1 to 3.5 is proven

text: Three new samples (lenses) of plastic material shall be subjected to five cycles of temperature and humidity change: (a) 3 hours at 40 °C ± 2 °C and 85-95 per cent RH; (b) 1 hour at 23 °C ± 5 °C and 60-75 per cent RH; (c) 15 hours at -30 °C ± 2 °C; (d) 1 hour at 23 °C ± 5 °C and 60-75 per cent RH; (e) 3 hours at 80 °C ± 2 °C; (f) 1 hour at 23 °C ± 5 °C and 60-75 per cent RH.
condition: resistance to temperature changes test

text: Before the temperature change test, the lens samples shall be kept at 23 °C ± 5 °C and 60-75 per cent RH for at least four hours.
condition: resistance to temperature changes test

text: The periods of one hour at 23 °C ± 5 °C shall include the periods of transition from one temperature to another needed to avoid thermal shock effects.
condition: resistance to temperature changes test

text: Photometric measurements shall be carried out on the lens samples before and after the temperature change test.
condition: resistance to temperature changes test

text: The photometric measurements for the temperature change test shall be made after photometric stability (as defined in UN Regulation No. 48) using a standard (étalon) light source, or with the light source(s) and/or light source module(s) as present in the road illumination device.
condition: resistance to temperature changes test

text: In the case of AFS, passing-beam of classes C and V, the measurements shall be made at B50L and 50R (B50R and 50L for headlamps intended for left-hand traffic).
condition: AFS or passing-beam of classes C and V

text: In the case of AFS and driving-beam of classes A and B, the measurement shall be made at Imax for the driving-beam.
condition: AFS or driving-beam of classes A and B

text: For Class BS headlamps, the passing-beam measurements shall be made at B50, 50L and 50R.
condition: Class BS headlamp

text: For Class CS and DS headlamps, the passing-beam or passing/driving lamp measurements shall be made at 0.86°D/3.5°R, 0.86°D/3.5°L, 0.50°U/1.5°L and 0.50°U/1.5°R.
condition: Class CS or DS headlamp

text: For classes BS, CS and DS, the measurement shall be made at Imax for the driving-beam of a driving lamp or a passing/driving lamp.
condition: Class BS, CS or DS driving-beam

text: For front fog lamps, the measurements shall be made at the intersection of the V-V line with line 6 and the intersection of the V-V line with line 4.
condition: front fog lamp

text: The variation between the photometric values measured on each sample before and after the temperature change test shall not exceed 10 per cent including the tolerances of the photometric procedure.

Three new samples (lenses or samples of material) shall be exposed to radiation from a source having a spectral energy distribution similar to that of a black body at a temperature between 5,500 K and 6,000 K.
condition: resistance to atmospheric agents test

text: Appropriate filters shall be placed between the source and the samples so as to reduce as far as possible radiations with wave lengths smaller than 295 nm and greater than 2,500 nm.
condition: resistance to atmospheric agents test

text: The samples shall be exposed to an energetic illumination of 1,200 W/m2 ± 200 W/m2 for a period such that the luminous energy received is equal to 4,500 MJ/m2 ± 200 MJ/m2.
condition: resistance to atmospheric agents test

text: Within the enclosure, the temperature measured on the black panel placed on a level with the samples shall be 50 °C ± 5 °C.
condition: resistance to atmospheric agents test

text: The samples shall revolve around the source of radiation at a speed between 1 and 5 1/min.
condition: resistance to atmospheric agents test

text: The samples shall be sprayed with distilled water of conductivity lower than 1 mS/m at a temperature of 23 °C ± 5 °C in the cycle: spraying 5 minutes; drying 25 minutes.
condition: resistance to atmospheric agents test

text: After the atmospheric agents test and the measurement of paragraph 3.2.3.1., the outer face of the three samples shall be treated as described in paragraph 3.2.2.2. with the mixture defined in paragraph 3.2.2.1.
condition: resistance to chemical agents test

text: The chemical agents test mixture shall be composed of 61.5 per cent n-heptane, 12.5 per cent toluene, 7.5 per cent ethyl tetrachloride, 12.5 per cent trichloroethylene and 6 per cent xylene (volume per cent).
condition: resistance to chemical agents test

text: A cotton cloth (as per ISO 105) soaked until saturation with the test mixture shall, within 10 seconds, be applied for 10 minutes to the outer face of the sample at a pressure of 50 N/cm2, corresponding to an effort of 100 N on a test surface of 14 mm x 14 mm.
condition: resistance to chemical agents test

text: During the 10-minute period, the cloth pad shall be soaked again with the mixture so that the composition of the liquid applied is continuously identical with that of the test mixture; compensation of the pressure to prevent cracks is permissible.
condition: resistance to chemical agents test

text: At the end of the application of the test mixture, the samples shall be dried in the open air, washed with the detergent solution of paragraph 3.4.1. at 23 °C ± 5 °C, rinsed with distilled water containing not more than 0.2 per cent impurities at 23 °C ± 5 °C and wiped off with a soft cloth.
condition: resistance to chemical agents test

text: After the test of resistance to atmospheric agents, the outer face of the samples shall be free from cracks, scratches, chipping and deformation.
After the test of resistance to atmospheric agents, the mean variation in transmission measured on the three samples according to Appendix 2 shall not exceed 0.020 (Δtm < 0.020).

After the test of resistance to chemical agents, the samples shall not bear any traces of chemical staining likely to cause a variation of flux diffusion, whose mean variation measured on the three samples according to Appendix 2 shall not exceed 0.020 (Δdm < 0.020).

If necessary, flat samples of each light transmitting plastic component of the road illumination device shall be exposed to the light of the light source(s), with angles and distances the same as in the road illumination device.
condition: unless light sources according to UN Regulation No. 37 and/or low-UV-type gas discharge light sources and/or low-UV-type LED modules are applied or components are shielded from UV radiation

text: The samples for the resistance to light source radiations test shall have the same colour and surface treatment, if any, as the parts of the road illumination device.
condition: resistance to light source radiations test

text: After 1,500 hours of continuous operation, the colorimetric requirements of the transmitted light must be met with a new light source.
condition: resistance to light source radiations test required

text: After 1,500 hours of continuous operation, the surfaces of the samples shall be free of cracks, scratches, scalings or deformation.
condition: resistance to light source radiations test required

text: The outer face of three samples (lenses or samples of material) shall be heated to 50 °C ± 5 °C and then immersed for five minutes in a mixture maintained at 23 °C ± 5 °C composed of 99 parts distilled water containing not more than 0.02 per cent impurities and one part alkylaryl sulphonate; afterwards the samples shall be dried at 50 °C ± 5 °C and cleaned with a moist cloth.
condition: resistance to detergents test

text: The outer face of the three samples shall then be lightly rubbed for one minute with a cotton cloth soaked in a mixture of 70 per cent n-heptane and 30 per cent toluene (volume per cent), and then dried in the open air.
condition: resistance to hydrocarbons test

text: After the detergent and hydrocarbon tests performed successively, the mean value of the variation in transmission measured on the three samples according to Appendix 2 shall not exceed 0.010 (Δtm < 0.010).
The outer face of three new samples (lenses) shall be subjected to the uniform mechanical deterioration test by the method described in Appendix 3.
After the mechanical deterioration test, the variations in transmission and diffusion shall be measured according to Appendix 2 in the area specified in paragraph 1.2.1.1.
After the mechanical deterioration test, the mean value of the variation in transmission of the three samples shall be Δtm < 0.100.
After the mechanical deterioration test, the mean value of the variation in diffusion of the three samples shall be Δdm < 0.050.
A surface of 20 mm x 20 mm of the coating of a lens shall be cut with a razor blade or a needle into a grid of squares approximately 2 mm x 2 mm, with pressure sufficient to cut at least the coating.
condition: if the lens has a coating

text: An adhesive tape at least 25 mm wide with a force adhesion of 2 N/(cm of width) ±20 per cent (measured per Appendix 4) shall be pressed for at least five minutes to the prepared surface, loaded perpendicular to the surface and torn off at a constant speed of 1.5 m/s ± 0.2 m/s.
condition: if the lens has a coating

text: There shall be no appreciable impairment of the gridded area of the coating; impairments at the intersections between squares or at the edges of the cuts are permitted provided that the impaired area does not exceed 15 per cent of the gridded surface.
condition: if the lens has a coating

text: The lens of complete road illumination device sample No. 1 shall be subjected to the mechanical deterioration test described in paragraph 3.5.1.
condition: device incorporating a lens of plastic material

text: For classes A, B and D and AFS, after the mechanical deterioration test the photometric measurements shall not exceed by more than 30 per cent the maximum values prescribed at point B50L (B50R for left-hand traffic).
condition: classes A, B and D and AFS with plastic lens

text: For classes A, B and D and AFS, after the mechanical deterioration test the photometric measurements shall not be more than 10 per cent below the minimum values prescribed at point 75R (75L for left-hand traffic).
condition: classes A, B and D and AFS with plastic lens

text: For a headlamp of classes A, B and D producing driving-beam only, after the mechanical deterioration test the photometric measurements shall not be more than 10 per cent below the minimum values prescribed for HV.
condition: headlamp producing driving-beam only

text: For Classes BS, CS and DS, after the mechanical deterioration test the photometric measurements shall not exceed by more than 30 per cent the maximum values prescribed at point HV.
condition: Classes BS, CS and DS with plastic lens

text: For Class BS headlamps, after the mechanical deterioration test the photometric values shall not be more than 10 per cent below the minimum values prescribed at points 50L and 50R.
condition: Class BS headlamp with plastic lens

text: For Classes CS and DS headlamps, after the mechanical deterioration test the photometric values shall not be more than 10 per cent below the minimum values prescribed at points 0.86°D/3.5°R and 0.86°D/3.5°L.
condition: Class CS or DS headlamp with plastic lens

text: For Classes BS, CS and DS headlamps producing driving-beam only, after the mechanical deterioration test the photometric values shall not be more than 10 per cent below the minimum values prescribed for HV.
condition: headlamp producing driving-beam only

text: For front fog lamps, after the mechanical deterioration test the photometric measurements prescribed for lines 2 and 5 shall not exceed the maximum values prescribed by more than 30 per cent.
condition: front fog lamp with plastic lens

text: The lens of complete device sample No. 2 shall be subjected to the coating adherence test described in paragraph 3.6.
condition: if the lens has a coating

text: For conformity of production of lens materials, after the tests for resistance to chemical agents and to detergents and hydrocarbons, the outer face of the samples shall exhibit no cracks, chipping or deformation visible to the naked eye.

For conformity of production, after the mechanical deterioration test of paragraph 3.7.1.1., the photometric values at the points of paragraph 3.7.1.2. shall be within the limits prescribed for conformity of production.
If the conformity of production test results fail to satisfy the requirements, the tests shall be repeated on another sample of road illumination devices selected at random.
condition: if test results fail

text: The lens or material samples shall be subjected to the material tests in the chronological order of Table A8-1, and complete device samples No. 1 and 2 to the deterioration, photometry and adherence tests of Table A8-2.

In the diffusion/transmission measurement equipment, the lens L2 diameter shall be such that it does not diaphragm the light diffused by the sample in a cone with a half top angle of 14°, it shall be possible to remove the central part of diaphragm DD and return it exactly to its original position, and the distance L2 Dτ and focal length of L2 shall be chosen so that the image of Dτ completely covers the receiver R.
condition: measurement of diffusion and transmission

text: When the initial incident flux is referred to 1,000 units, the absolute precision of each reading shall be better than 1 unit.
condition: measurement of diffusion and transmission

text: Readings T1 to T5 of Table A8-3 (incident flux, transmitted flux and diffused flux of the new and tested material) shall be taken.
condition: measurement of diffusion and transmission

text: The spray gun shall be equipped with a nozzle 1.3 mm in diameter allowing a liquid flow rate of 0.24 ± 0.02 l/minute at an operating pressure of 6.0 bars -0/+0.5 bar, giving a fan pattern of 170 mm ± 50 mm in diameter at a distance of 380 mm ± 10 mm from the nozzle.
condition: spray testing method

text: The spray test mixture shall be composed of silica sand of hardness 7 on the Mohr scale, grain size between 0 and 0.2 mm, almost normal distribution, angular factor 1.8 to 2, and water of hardness not exceeding 205 g/m3, with 25 g of sand per litre of water.
condition: spray testing method

text: The outer surface of the lamp lenses shall be subjected once or more to the sand jet sprayed almost perpendicular to the surface, with deterioration checked by reference glass samples placed near the lenses, until the specified variation in diffusion on the reference samples is reached.
condition: spray testing method

text: The ambient conditions for the adhesive tape adherence test shall be 23 °C ± 5 °C and 65 ± 15 per cent RH.
condition: adhesive tape adherence test

text: Before the test, the sample roll of adhesive tape shall be conditioned for 24 hours in the specified atmosphere, and five test pieces each 400 mm long shall be tested from each roll, taken after the first three turns were discarded.
condition: adhesive tape adherence test

text: The test pieces shall be unrolled at approximately 300 mm/s, applied to the glass plate within 15 seconds without air bubbles, left for 10 minutes in the specified atmosphere, and pulled off at 90° at a speed of 300 mm/s ± 30 mm/s while recording the force required.
condition: adhesive tape adherence test

text: The five values obtained shall be arranged in order and the median value taken as the result, expressed in Newtons per centimetre of width of the tape.
condition: adhesive tape adherence test

text: Each LED module sample submitted shall conform to the relevant requirements of this Regulation when tested with the supplied electronic light source control-gear(s), if any.
LED module(s) shall be so designed as to be and to remain in good working order when in normal use.
LED module(s) shall exhibit no fault in design or manufacture.
The LED(s) on the LED module shall be equipped with suitable fixation elements.
The fixation elements shall be strong and firmly secured to the LED(s) and the LED module.
All LED module samples shall be tested as specified in paragraph 4 of Annex 9.
All LED module samples shall be tested under the conditions as specified in paragraphs 4.6.2.1.1. and 4.6.2.2.1. of this Regulation.
For the measurement of electrical and photometric characteristics, the LED module device shall be operated in a dry and still atmosphere at an ambient temperature of 23 °C ± 5 °C.
Upon the request of the applicant the LED module shall be operated for 15 h and cooled down to ambient temperature before starting the tests as specified in this Regulation.
condition: upon the request of the applicant

text: In addition to paragraph 4.16, the light of a LED module, when tested outside the device, shall meet the minimum red content requirement, calculated using intervals of one nanometre.

The UV-radiation of a low-UV-type LED module, when tested outside the device, shall meet the specified UV-radiation limit, calculated using intervals of one nanometre with km = 683 lm/W and weighted according to the S(λ) values in Table A9-1.
condition: if the LED module is of low-UV type

text: For measurement of the objective luminous flux of LED module(s) producing the principal passing-beam, the LED module(s) shall be in the configuration as described in the technical specification defined in paragraph 3.1.2.2.
condition: LED module(s) producing the principal passing-beam

text: Optical elements (secondary optics) shall be removed by the Technical Service at the request of the applicant by the use of tools.
condition: at the request of the applicant

text: The secondary optics removal procedure and the conditions during the objective luminous flux measurements shall be described in the test report.
One LED module of each type shall be submitted by the applicant with the electronic light source control gear, if applicable, and sufficient instructions.
Before the objective luminous flux test each LED module shall be aged at least for seventy-two hours under the same conditions as in the corresponding headlamp application.
In the case of use of an integrating sphere, the sphere shall have a minimum diameter of one meter, and at least ten times the maximum dimension of the LED module, whichever is the largest.
condition: if an integrating sphere is used

text: The prescriptions in CIE - Publication 84 - 1989, regarding the room temperature, positioning, etc., shall be taken into consideration for LED module flux measurement.
The LED module shall be burned in for approximately one hour in the closed sphere or goniophotometer, and the flux shall be measured after photometric stability has occurred.
The luminous intensity distribution and the colour of the light emitted shall be measured and checked for compliance after photometric stability (as defined in UN Regulation No. 48).
For cornering lamps, the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
condition: lamps (functions) using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only

text: For all lamps other than cornering lamps, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and after photometric stability shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
condition: lamps (functions) using light source technologies other than incandescent technology only

text: A driving-beam (headlamp producing only driving-beam) shall be checked for compliance at 1 second after activation at test point HV.
condition: depending on the light source technology

text: A passing-beam shall be checked for compliance at 4 seconds after activation at test point 25V (V, 1.72°D), and after 1 second it shall meet at least 25 % of the requirement at the test point.
condition: depending on the light source technology

text: An AFS class C passing-beam shall be checked for compliance at 4 seconds after activation at test point 25V (V, 1.72°D), and after 1 second it shall meet at least 25 % of the requirement at the test point.
condition: depending on the light source technology

text: A front fog lamp shall be checked for compliance at 4 seconds after activation at test point V, 2.5°D.
condition: depending on the light source technology

text: A cornering lamp shall be checked for compliance at 1 second after activation at test point 45°L 2.5°D resp. 45°R 2.5°D.
condition: depending on the light source technology

text: A lamp (function) using incandescent technology only is deemed to comply with the intensity requirements at all points in time if the values measured after photometric stability are compliant.
condition: incandescent technology only

text: A lamp (function) using gas-discharge technology only is deemed to comply with the intensity requirements at all points in time if the values measured at the point in time according to Table A10-1 and after photometric stability are compliant.
condition: gas-discharge technology only

text: A lamp (function) using LED technology only is deemed to comply with the intensity requirements at all points in time if the values measured at 1 minute after activation and after photometric stability are compliant.
condition: LED technology only

text: For any other light generating technology, the intensity requirements of a lamp (function) shall be tested and checked for compliance at all points in time starting at the point in time listed in Table A10-1 and ending when photometric stability is reached.
condition: other light generating technology

text: For a lamp (function) using more than one light generating technology, the intensity requirements shall be tested following the strictest time requirements according to paragraphs 2.1.1. to 2.1.4. for the combination and checked for compliance.
condition: more than one light generating technology

text: In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), the minimum intensity requirements of a lamp (function) shall additionally be tested and checked for compliance at all points in time starting at the point in time listed in Table A10-1.
condition: in case of doubt

text: The optional centre of reference mark, if used, shall be positioned on the lens at its intersection with the reference axis of the passing-beam, also on the lenses of driving-beams and/or cornering lamps when neither grouped, combined nor reciprocally incorporated with a passing-beam, and on the lens of a front fog lamp, with dimension a = 2 mm min.
condition: if the centre of reference mark is used

text: The voltage marking required by paragraph 3.3.4.6. shall conform to Figure A12.
condition: AFS, front fog lamps and headlamps meeting Annex 7 only when supplied at 12V

text: The AFS description form No. 1 shall indicate the AFS control signals relevant to the lighting functions and modes, marking the applicable combinations with a cross (X).

The technical characteristics of each AFS control signal shall be indicated in terms of physical nature, information type, time dependent properties, signal status when the conditions of paragraph 6.22.7.4. of UN R48 or 6.18.6.3. of UN R53 are fulfilled, and signal status in case of failure.
The AFS description form No. 2 shall indicate for each lighting unit its cut-off status, vertical and horizontal adjustment devices (individual/master or linked) and adjustment procedures.
